item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Since assuming the presidency, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi assigned the military to manage a widening range of civilian national projects and expanded its role in economic policy-setting, viewing the military as the most competent and loyal state agency for delivering desired results.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The source describes policy established since 2014 and continuing through the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the expansion and delegation choices to Sisi.","limitations":["The source is a 2024 analysis and does not provide a complete 2023 administrative record."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Military-managed civilian projects operated with substantial autonomy in project design, licensing, partner selection, and subcontracting; the source found no hard evidence that the military monitored environmental compliance.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","6B.5","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source presents this as the operational condition surrounding projects during the relevant period.","ruler_attribution":"The source links the military's expanded civilian role to Sisi's governing approach but does not document a specific 2023 order.","limitations":["The finding is an analytical assessment of available evidence, not a disclosed audit result."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Egypt issued multiple climate and sectoral strategies, including the National Strategy for Climate Change 2050, but cited assessments found weak implementation mechanisms, inadequate institutional capacity, insufficient funding, limited civil-society and private-sector roles, and poor interagency coordination.","question_ids":["1B.9","5B.7","6B.5","6B.9","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The strategy summary was released in 2022 and the implementation shortcomings remained relevant during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The strategy was issued by Egyptian state authorities under Sisi's administration.","limitations":["The source reports expert and civil-society assessments rather than a complete government evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Military activities and project data, including environmental impacts and environmental impact assessments, were largely inaccessible; the military was legally exempt from civilian financial disclosure, treated civilian-domain activities as covered by a national-security firewall, and a 2021 Penal Code amendment criminalized collecting armed-forces information without Defense Ministry consent.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","5B.7","6B.5","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The legal and disclosure restrictions were in force during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the broad military exemption and the 2021 amendment to state policy under the Sisi-era system.","limitations":["The source does not identify a personal Sisi directive for each restriction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A World Bank study released in 2023 credited improved public transport with reducing air pollution in Greater Cairo by 4 percent and estimated avoided-mortality gains at approximately $110.4 million.","question_ids":["5B.6","6B.2","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The study and reported result are explicitly from 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The result concerns government transport policy during Sisi's administration; the source does not establish that Sisi personally caused the entire effect.","limitations":["The source does not specify which projects produced the measured reduction or establish the precise causal contribution of Sisi personally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Military aquaculture and livestock projects increased total fish production by nearly 18 percent between 2016 and 2020, while Egypt continued importing about half of its food needs.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The quantitative production result predates 2023 but formed part of the administration's continuing food-security program.","ruler_attribution":"The projects were military-managed under Sisi's administration.","limitations":["The source does not establish the projects' distributional effects or their exact contribution to national food security in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Egypt's annual water deficit reached approximately 7 billion cubic meters, nearly 10 percent of total demand, in 2023; strategic-crop yields such as wheat and corn declined by 30–40 percent in 2023, while the orange harvest was nearly ruined.","question_ids":["5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The water deficit and crop results are explicitly reported for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"These were national outcomes during Sisi's presidency; the source attributes them to combined mismanagement, resource pressures, and climate change rather than solely to Sisi.","limitations":["The source does not provide a counterfactual isolating policy responsibility from climate and inherited conditions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Egypt's June 2023 updated climate commitments targeted rehabilitation of 20,000 kilometers of irrigation canals, expanded reuse of agricultural drainage and treated wastewater, and construction of large desalination and treatment plants; military agencies were implementing much of this work.","question_ids":["1B.9","5B.6","6B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The commitments were issued in June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The commitments were made by Egypt's government during Sisi's presidency; the source does not identify the precise presidential approval process.","limitations":["The source describes targets and implementation activity but does not establish completion or outcome by the end of 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The government pursued 37 new cities, while studies demonstrating the need for the cities were not released and parliament had not discussed the megaprojects; as of March 2023, necessary environmental studies for Egypt's cities and towns were still absent and the Housing Ministry had not revised plans for expected climate disruptions.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.6","5B.6","5B.7","6B.5","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The absence of environmental studies and unrevised plans is explicitly reported as of March 2023; the city program was ongoing in the period.","ruler_attribution":"The urban-development strategy and megaproject agenda are attributed to the Sisi administration.","limitations":["The source does not identify every project covered by the stated absence of studies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The subsidized Social Housing Project, intended to provide one million affordable units during 2011–2016, delivered 215,000 units; research found access for precarious or poor households largely theoretical, while new-city vacancies commonly exceeded 70 percent and only 1.6 million people lived in all new cities completed by 2017.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The figures predate 2023 but describe the inherited and continuing housing-policy record relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The housing and new-city strategy continued under Sisi's administration.","limitations":["Some outcome figures are historical and do not measure changes during 2023 itself."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"By 2020, 83 percent of Cairo's population had less than 1.5 square meters of green space per person, far below the World Health Organization's 9-square-meter recommendation; 14.5 billion Egyptian pounds were spent on sports facilities in 2018–2023 compared with $2.8 billion for a new Olympic City in the New Administrative Capital.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The spending comparison covers 2018–2023; the green-space measure is from 2020 and remained relevant to the period.","ruler_attribution":"The investment choices occurred under Sisi's administration.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the Olympic City expenditure was executed entirely in 2023 or quantify its direct welfare effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Transport accounted for 40 percent of Egypt's carbon emissions in 2021; transport-sector emissions grew 14.7 percent in the year to mid-2023, and continued road expansion was projected to increase carbon emissions by 37 percent by 2030. Sisi designated 52 national roads as strategic military-importance zones between 2016 and 2023.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.9","5B.6","5B.9","8B.2","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The emissions increase and road-designation endpoint are explicitly linked to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the road designations to Sisi and describes the broader transport strategy as his administration's approach.","limitations":["The projected 2030 increase is not an observed outcome, and the source does not quantify the emissions effect of the military designation itself."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"The military-managed New Administrative Capital depended entirely on diverted water from other cities, and a dedicated water-treatment plant cost 40 billion Egyptian pounds, nearly as much as Egypt's total investment in potable water and sanitation in 2022–2023.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The comparison uses the 2022–2023 investment period and describes an ongoing project during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The New Administrative Capital and its water infrastructure were central projects of the Sisi administration and were military-managed.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the spending displaced other projects or measure service access for ordinary residents."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"Satellite-based research found all Egyptian aquifers undergoing significant storage loss, with groundwater pumped without rationing restrictions; monitoring networks were insufficient and pumping reports were treated as sensitive or confidential. Researchers also reported that no feasibility studies were conducted for major agricultural schemes and discussion before implementation was shut down.","question_ids":["1B.9","4B.3","4B.6","5B.7","6B.5","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The evidence includes data through 2021 and describes conditions continuing into the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The schemes and restrictions operated under Sisi's administration; the source does not attribute each operational decision personally to him.","limitations":["The source relies on cited studies and researcher claims and does not provide a complete 2023 monitoring dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Military-managed desert cultivation relied on intensive groundwater extraction and chemical fertilizers; a 2024 comparison found wheat yields of 3 metric tons per feddan in military-managed schemes versus 4.05 tons in Damietta and 4.5 tons in Qena on unreclaimed land, while researchers warned of aquifer depletion, salinity, contamination, and long-term land degradation.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The schemes were active during the 2023 period; the yield comparison is from April 2024 and is retrospective.","ruler_attribution":"The schemes were undertaken by the Sisi administration and managed by military entities.","limitations":["The yield comparison is post-period evidence and does not isolate weather, crop, or input differences."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Military companies held approximately one-quarter of Egypt's cement production capacity and 16 percent of steel capacity, continued using coal-fired furnaces, and operated in highly polluting chemical, fertilizer, mineral, and metallurgical sectors; financial and environmental data on these activities were inaccessible.","question_ids":["1B.9","4B.6","5B.5","5B.7","6B.5","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The industrial position and information-access conditions describe the Sisi-era system continuing into the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The military's industrial expansion and state-directed projects occurred under Sisi's administration.","limitations":["The source does not provide a 2023 production audit or establish Sisi's personal involvement in each company decision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69c10f5da4922507","start_unit":16,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"The government pledged in November 2022 to subject economically active military entities to the same fiscal-transparency and reporting standards as other state-owned enterprises and economic authorities, but the source recommended extending comparable transparency and environmental-audit requirements because environmental data remained unavailable.","question_ids":["4B.6","5B.5","5B.7","6B.5","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The pledge preceded and its implementation status was relevant during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The pledge was made by the Sisi government; the source does not establish full implementation during 2023.","limitations":["The source does not document whether the pledge produced completed disclosures or audits by the end of 2023."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The document is a 2024 retrospective policy analysis, so several facts describe policies, outcomes, or institutional conditions established before or continuing through 2023 rather than events occurring solely in 2023.","The source emphasizes environmental governance and military-managed civilian projects; it provides little or no material evidence about nuclear weapons, conventional war, detention, elections, personal financial integrity, or ordinary public truthfulness."]}
